saints.name: Symeon Metaphrastes
saints.dates: Tenth century; traditional Prologue dates his repose to about 960

summary.text: A Byzantine compiler of saints’ lives whose name also appears in Orthodox Communion prayers. He is distinct from Saint Symeon the New Theologian.
summary.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

saints.context: The Church's published hagiographic account is distinguished from independently established chronology. Unknown dates and circumstances are left unspecified.

blocks.text: The Prologue portrays Symeon as a learned Constantinopolitan who served at the imperial court before retiring from secular work. Its details belong to a received hagiographic account.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: His enduring work was the collection and literary revision of saints’ biographies. The OCA’s introductory catechesis places the beginning of his compilation in the tenth century and explains how such narratives are organized for liturgical remembrance.
blocks.locator: Page 72, The Lives of the Saints

blocks.text: The Prologue dates his repose to about 960 and reports myrrh associated with his body. It does not describe an execution. The approximate date is retained as that source’s chronology.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: The GOARCH Synekdemos includes a Communion preparation prayer under his name. Hagiography and prayer attribution explain why a learner encounters him in both saints’ lives and prayer books.

researchNotes: November 9 is explicitly given by the ROCOR parish Menaion and by OCA saint-life references to him. Some other calendars commemorate November 28. The profile follows the cited Russian-tradition Menaion.
Do not conflate Symeon Metaphrastes with Saint Symeon the New Theologian. Exact court offices, work totals and a precise death year are not asserted here.
